audit_findings.title: The earnings numerator and 575.329 million-share denominator may represent different economic claims
audit_findings.magnitude: $234.575 million 2025 diluted-EPS numerator reallocation, equal to 30.4% of the $770.947 million basic numerator; owner-earnings correction unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The denominator includes exchangeable RP Holdings Class B and eligible Class E interests, while plc-attributable owner earnings exclude income allocated to those interests.
audit_findings.evidence: Our outstanding Class B ordinary shares are considered potentially dilutive shares of Class A ordinary shares because Class B ordinary shares, together with the related RP Holdings Class B Interests and vested RP Holdings Class E Interests, are exchangeable into Class A ordinary shares on a one -for-one basis.
audit_findings.explanation: The claim-perimeter mismatch is demonstrated by the filing's diluted-EPS reconciliation. Its exact effect on owner earnings remains unresolved, but the filed earnings reallocation is large enough to affect per-share value materially.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $747.5 million owner-earnings anchor to an if-converted numerator, adding the owner earnings attributable to every Class B and Class E interest included in the 575.329 million denominator, then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Consolidated adjustments and bridge assets may include legacy-NCI economics absent from the denominator
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately $1.503 billion of latest filed financial-royalty-asset fair value is attributable to legacy NCI, computed as 9% of $0.9 billion plus 6% of $23.7 billion; actual valuation correction unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Legacy-NCI portions can enter consolidated owner-earnings adjustments or the cash and stakes bridge even though legacy investors are absent from the share denominator.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, approximately 7 % of the current portion and 7 % of the non-current portion of the financial royalty assets was attributable to the legacy non-controlling interests.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved attribution possibility, not a demonstrated model error. The filing already nets legacy distributions from Portfolio Receipts, but the supplied record does not show whether every consolidated adjustment and bridge asset was similarly attributed. The approximately $1.503 billion asset scale is 12.3% of base equity value and therefore potentially material.
audit_findings.action: Prepare an entity-by-entity schedule for each owner-earnings adjustment, cash balance, security and equity-method stake; remove legacy-NCI portions and rerun if any are presently included.

audit_findings.title: A material Employee EPA liability may be an unbridged claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $713.219 million latest filed liability, equal to $1.24 per modeled share and 5.8% of $12.215 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any Employee EPA settlement obligation not already captured through future compensation expense or share dilution must reduce the equity bridge or owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the fair value of Employee EPAs was $ 577.9 million as recorded within Accrued compensation liabilities on the consolidated balance sheet.
audit_findings.explanation: Omission of the latest Employee EPA liability from the listed bridge is demonstrated. The net valuation error remains unresolved because the record does not identify how much is already reflected in owner earnings, future compensation expense, EPA payments or the fully diluted denominator. The gross liability is large enough to be material.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $713.219 million liability to vested and unvested awards, expected cash and share settlement, OE compensation deductions and denominator dilution; bridge only the residual claim and rerun.

audit_findings.title: The $901 million stakes bridge may double-count operating portfolio assets
audit_findings.magnitude: $901.0 million bridge addition, equal to $1.57 per share and 7.4% of base equity value; related capitalized numerator overlap unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Available-for-sale funding assets and equity-method interests may contribute receipts or earnings to owner earnings while their asset value is also added through stakes_net.
audit_findings.evidence: Portfolio Receipts is calculated as the sum of the following line items from our GAAP consolidated statements of cash flows: Cash collections from financial royalty assets , Cash collections from intangible royalty assets , Other royalty cash collections , Proceeds from available for sale debt securities and Distributions from equity method investees less Distributions to legacy non-controlling interests - Portfolio Receipts , which represent contractual distributions of Royalty Receipts, milestones and other contractual receipts to the Legacy Investors Partnerships.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that Portfolio Receipts can include available-for-sale proceeds and equity-method distributions, but the supplied owner-earnings reconciliation does not establish whether those contributions were purged. A full $901 million bridge duplication alone would be material, and capitalization of overlapping recurring receipts could increase the error.
audit_findings.action: List every stakes_net component and trace its interest, gains, earnings, proceeds and distributions through the 2025 OE calculation; remove either each bridge asset or its corresponding numerator contribution and rerun.

audit_findings.title: Perpetual growth may be unfunded because royalty acquisitions function as replacement investment
audit_findings.magnitude: $2,497.031 million average annual capital deployment for 2021-2025, equal to 3.34 times the $747.5 million anchor OE; replacement portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Replacement acquisitions and development funding required to offset finite royalty expirations are reinvestment needed to sustain OE and terminal growth, rather than freely distributable owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: Ongoing investment in new royalties is fundamental to the long-term prospects of our business.
audit_findings.explanation: The conflict between finite royalty lives and an unfunded 2.5% perpetual-growth terminal value is demonstrated, while the amount of capital deployment that is replacement rather than incremental remains unresolved. Because recent annual deployment substantially exceeds anchor OE and terminal value supplies roughly half of operating value, the issue is reasonably capable of materially changing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Construct a royalty-expiration runoff and separate historical and forecast capital deployment into replacement and incremental investment; deduct required replacement investment from OE or model it explicitly before recomputing terminal value.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 anchor may retain a large noncash provision reversal
audit_findings.magnitude: $295.838 million, equal to 39.6% of anchor OE; if fully retained, computed base-case sensitivity is approximately $4.155 billion or $7.22 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: A noncash provision credit retained in the latest-actual OE anchor is projected and capitalized through the explicit forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2025, we recorded provision income of $295.8 million, comprised of $269.7 million in provision income for changes in expected cash flows and $26.2 million in provision income for current expected credit losses.
audit_findings.explanation: The provision credit is filed and clearly noncash, but its retention in owner earnings is only an unresolved possibility because the exact OE reconciliation was not supplied. If retained, its size relative to the anchor makes the resulting overstatement material.
audit_findings.action: Produce the complete 2025 OE reconciliation, verify that the $295.838 million credit was removed, confirm symmetrical treatment of provision expenses and reversals in every historical year, and rerun all scenarios if it was retained.
